body.statement: Conditional on an affirmative resolution of \texttt{oeq:polytope-maximal-inequality} establishing \[\mathbb E_{\Pr_{P,\rho,b,o}}\sup_{q\in\Theta(P)}|M_T(q)|\le \frac{511B d^{dk}}{\epsilon}\sqrt T\] uniformly over \(\mathfrak M_{d,k,T}(\epsilon,B)\), every \(T\ge1\), initial law \(\rho\), and deterministic observation map \(o\) satisfy \[\mathbb E_{\Pr_{P,\rho,b,o}}[D_T(P,\rho,b,o,E_T)]\le\min\left\{1,\frac{C_{d,k,\epsilon,B}}{\sqrt T}\right\},\qquad C_{d,k,\epsilon,B}=\frac{1024B d^{dk}}{\epsilon}.\] The implication imposes no lower bound on any coordinate of \(q\) and no contraction condition on \(L_q\).
body.justification: This conditional implication states the dimension-explicit sample-length certificate delivered only after the mandatory square and whole-polytope obligations are resolved.
body.gap: HaughSingal2026Casino, arXiv version 3, pages 9--11, Sections 4.2--4.3, shows only that in its special casino model the time-homogeneous and time-inhomogeneous \(\mathrm{EWAC}/T\) bounds converge together as \(T\to\infty\); it supplies neither a finite root-\(T\) rate nor a bound uniform over the complete finite-state stationary response-program fiber. LallyKazemiPaoletti2026RobustCounterfactualMDP is sharp one transition at a time, HaughSingal2023DynamicLatent gives finite-record programs, and SayedanaCainesMahajan2025 controls one fixed kernel; none supplies the stated whole-polytope premise.
body.consumer: An affirmative open-question result turns this implication into a sample-length certificate for robust trajectory attribution and policy auditing.
body.proof_tex:
Assume the displayed premise of the theorem, namely
\[
 \mathbb E_{\Pr_{P,\rho,b,o}}\sup_{q\in\Theta(P)}|M_T(q)|
 \le \frac{511B d^{dk}}{\epsilon}\sqrt T.
\]
Write \(m=d^{dk}\).  By the Poisson-martingale identity and the fact that both \(\alpha_0(q)K_{\pi}h\) and \(\alpha_T(q)K_{\pi}h\) lie in \([0,B]\), every positive-probability full record satisfies
\[
 \left|Q^{\mathrm{full}}_{q,T}(X_{0:T})-g\right|
 \le \frac{B+|M_T(q)|}{T}.
\]
Therefore
\[
\begin{aligned}
 D^{\mathrm{full}}_T(P,\rho,b,X_{0:T})
 &\le 2\sup_{q\in\Theta(P)}
 \left|Q^{\mathrm{full}}_{q,T}(X_{0:T})-g\right|\\
 &\le \frac{2B}{T}+\frac{2}{T}\sup_{q\in\Theta(P)}|M_T(q)|.
\end{aligned}
\]
Taking expectations, applying the assumed maximal inequality, and using \(T\ge1\), \(m\ge1\), and \(0<\epsilon\le1\), gives
\[
\begin{aligned}
 \mathbb E D^{\mathrm{full}}_T(P,\rho,b,X_{0:T})
 &\le \frac{2B}{T}+\frac{1022Bm}{\epsilon\sqrt T}\\
 &\le \frac{2Bm}{\epsilon\sqrt T}
       +\frac{1022Bm}{\epsilon\sqrt T}
 =\frac{1024B d^{dk}}{\epsilon\sqrt T}
 =\frac{C_{d,k,\epsilon,B}}{\sqrt T}.
\end{aligned}
\]
The coarsening-domination lemma transfers this bound to
\(\mathbb E D_T(P,\rho,b,o,E_T)\).  Since \(0\le r\le1\), every conditional average reward belongs to \([0,1]\), so every identified-interval diameter is also at most one.  Taking the smaller of the two valid upper bounds proves the theorem.  The argument nowhere divides by a response mass \(q_f\) and nowhere invokes contraction of \(L_q\); the only asserted maximal inequality is precisely the theorem's explicit conditional premise.
